1	"""Read-only audit replication batches.
2	
3	A batch is a single UTF-8 compact JSON object (non-ASCII preserved, no
4	whitespace) terminated by exactly one ``\\n``::
5	
6	    {"after":...,"complete":...,"next":...,"records":[...],"version":1}
7	
8	The top-level keys are fixed in the order ``after``, ``complete``,
9	``next``, ``records``, ``version`` and ``version`` is always the integer
10	1.  ``after`` echoes the request's ``after`` argument.  ``records`` holds
11	up to ``limit`` (at most 1000) audit records whose ``seq`` is greater
12	than ``after``, in audit order, each preserving the audit record key
13	order ``detail, hash, kind, prev, seq, source`` and its original values.
14	``next`` is the seq of the last record in the batch, or ``after`` itself
15	when the batch is empty; ``complete`` is true when no record follows the
16	batch, and an empty ``records`` list is only valid when ``complete`` is
17	true.  Batches are generated solely through :func:`audit.read`, so the
18	audit log is never modified and :class:`~offline_coordination.audit.
19	CorruptAuditError` and :class:`OSError` propagate unchanged.
20	
21	:func:`import_batch` validates a batch against this byte contract and
22	appends its records to the local log.  It returns a dict with the fixed
23	key order ``need``, ``next``, ``status``.  When the batch starts beyond
24	the local log (``after`` greater than the local last seq ``L``) nothing is
25	written and ``status`` is ``"missing"`` with ``need`` holding the gap
26	``[L + 1, after]`` and ``next`` set to ``L``.  Otherwise records already
27	present locally must match field by field (a mismatch raises
28	:class:`ValueError`); the matching prefix is skipped idempotently and
29	only the contiguous suffix past ``L`` is appended, linked to the local
30	last hash.  ``need`` is then ``None``, ``next`` is ``max(L, batch.next)``
31	and ``status`` is ``"applied"`` when records were appended, else
32	``"duplicate"``.  Any failure leaves the log untouched.
33	
34	Batch records are checked only against the byte contract: canonical
35	encoding, key order, the seq/prev/hash chain and the stored values.
36	Value-domain rules enforced by :func:`audit.append` on event input (the
37	kind enum, non-empty string fields) are *not* re-enforced here, so every
38	log :func:`audit.read` accepts round-trips through
39	:func:`export_batch`/:func:`import_batch`.  The append itself is atomic:
40	when the write, flush or fsync step raises :class:`OSError` the error
41	propagates unchanged and the log is left byte-identical to its pre-call
42	state (still missing when it was missing).
43	"""
44	
45	from __future__ import annotations
46	
47	import json
48	import os
49	import re
50	
51	from offline_coordination import audit
52	
53	AFTER = "after"
54	COMPLETE = "complete"
55	NEED = "need"
56	NEXT = "next"
57	RECORDS = "records"
58	STATUS = "status"
59	VERSION = "version"
60	
61	STATUS_MISSING = "missing"
62	STATUS_APPLIED = "applied"
63	STATUS_DUPLICATE = "duplicate"
64	
65	_BATCH_KEYS = (AFTER, COMPLETE, NEXT, RECORDS, VERSION)
66	_RESULT_KEYS = (NEED, NEXT, STATUS)
67	_RECORD_KEYS = (
68	    audit.DETAIL,
69	    audit.HASH,
70	    audit.KIND,
71	    audit.PREV,
72	    audit.SEQ,
73	    audit.SOURCE,
74	)
75	_BATCH_VERSION = 1
76	_MIN_LIMIT = 1
77	_MAX_LIMIT = 1000
78	_HEX64 = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{64}")
79	
80	
81	def export_batch(path: str, after: int = 0, limit: int = 100) -> bytes:
82	    """Return one replication batch of audit records as UTF-8 JSON bytes.
83	
84	    Selects the first ``limit`` records whose ``seq`` is greater than
85	    ``after``.  ``after`` must not exceed the log's last seq (an empty or
86	    missing log has last seq 0); otherwise :class:`ValueError` is raised.
87	
88	    Type violations raise :class:`TypeError` (``bool`` is not accepted as
89	    an int); ``after < 0`` or a ``limit`` outside ``[1, 1000]`` raises
90	    :class:`ValueError`.  A corrupt log raises
91	    :class:`~offline_coordination.audit.CorruptAuditError` and filesystem
92	    errors propagate as :class:`OSError`.  The log is never modified.
93	    """
94	    if not isinstance(path, str):
95	        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
96	    if isinstance(after, bool) or not isinstance(after, int):
97	        raise TypeError("after must be an int")
98	    if isinstance(limit, bool) or not isinstance(limit, int):
99	        raise TypeError("limit must be an int")
100	    if after < 0:
101	        raise ValueError("after must be >= 0")
102	    if limit < _MIN_LIMIT or limit > _MAX_LIMIT:
103	        raise ValueError("limit must be in [1, 1000]")
104	
105	    all_records = audit.read(path)
106	    last_seq = all_records[-1][audit.SEQ] if all_records else 0
107	    if after > last_seq:
108	        raise ValueError("after must not exceed the last audit seq")
109	
110	    selected = [record for record in all_records if record[audit.SEQ] > after]
111	    selected = selected[:limit]
112	    batch_records = [
113	        {key: record[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS} for record in selected
114	    ]
115	
116	    next_seq = batch_records[-1][audit.SEQ] if batch_records else after
117	    batch = {
118	        AFTER: after,
119	        COMPLETE: next_seq == last_seq,
120	        NEXT: next_seq,
121	        RECORDS: batch_records,
122	        VERSION: _BATCH_VERSION,
123	    }
124	    ordered = {key: batch[key] for key in _BATCH_KEYS}
125	    text = json.dumps(ordered, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
126	    return text.encode("utf-8")
127	
128	
129	def _invalid_batch(message: str) -> ValueError:
130	    return ValueError(f"invalid replication batch: {message}")
131	
132	
133	def _compact(obj: object) -> bytes:
134	    return json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
135	
136	
137	def _parse_batch(batch: bytes) -> dict:
138	    """Validate a batch against the export byte contract and decode it."""
139	    if not batch.endswith(b"\n") or batch.endswith(b"\n\n"):
140	        raise _invalid_batch("must be a single JSON object terminated by one LF")
141	    try:
142	        data = json.loads(batch[:-1].decode("utf-8"))
143	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
144	        raise _invalid_batch("is not valid UTF-8 JSON") from exc
145	
146	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or tuple(data.keys()) != _BATCH_KEYS:
147	        raise _invalid_batch(
148	            "top-level object must have exactly the keys "
149	            "'after', 'complete', 'next', 'records', 'version' in order"
150	        )
151	    version = data[VERSION]
152	    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int) or version != _BATCH_VERSION:
153	        raise _invalid_batch("version must be the integer 1")
154	    for key in (AFTER, NEXT):
155	        if isinstance(data[key], bool) or not isinstance(data[key], int):
156	            raise _invalid_batch(f"{key} must be an int")
157	        if data[key] < 0:
158	            raise _invalid_batch(f"{key} must be >= 0")
159	    if not isinstance(data[COMPLETE], bool):
160	        raise _invalid_batch("complete must be a bool")
161	    records = data[RECORDS]
162	    if not isinstance(records, list):
163	        raise _invalid_batch("records must be a list")
164	    if len(records) > _MAX_LIMIT:
165	        raise _invalid_batch("records must contain at most 1000 items")
166	    if not records and not data[COMPLETE]:
167	        raise _invalid_batch("empty records require complete to be true")
168	
169	    expected_seq = data[AFTER]
170	    expected_prev = audit._ZERO_HASH if data[AFTER] == 0 else None
171	    for index, record in enumerate(records):
172	        if not isinstance(record, dict) or tuple(record.keys()) != _RECORD_KEYS:
173	            raise _invalid_batch(
174	                f"record {index} must have exactly the keys "
175	                "'detail', 'hash', 'kind', 'prev', 'seq', 'source' in order"
176	            )
177	        # Only the byte contract is enforced here: key order, the
178	        # seq/prev/hash chain and the stored values.  Value-domain rules
179	        # (non-empty fields, the kind enum) belong to audit.append's event
180	        # input, so records from any log audit.read accepts stay importable.
181	        prev = record[audit.PREV]
182	        digest = record[audit.HASH]
183	        if expected_prev is not None:
184	            if prev != expected_prev:
185	                raise _invalid_batch(
186	                    f"record {index} prev does not match the previous record hash"
187	                )
188	        elif not isinstance(prev, str) or not _HEX64.fullmatch(prev):
189	            # The first record's prev refers to the exporter's log and
190	            # cannot be checked against local state; require hash shape.
191	            raise _invalid_batch(f"record {index} prev must be 64 lowercase hex chars")
192	        seq = record[audit.SEQ]
193	        if isinstance(seq, bool) or not isinstance(seq, int):
194	            raise _invalid_batch(f"record {index} seq must be an int")
195	        expected_seq += 1
196	        if seq != expected_seq:
197	            raise _invalid_batch(
198	                f"record {index} seq is {seq}, expected {expected_seq}"
199	            )
200	        without_hash = {
201	            audit.DETAIL: record[audit.DETAIL],
202	            audit.KIND: record[audit.KIND],
203	            audit.PREV: prev,
204	            audit.SEQ: seq,
205	            audit.SOURCE: record[audit.SOURCE],
206	        }
207	        if digest != audit._record_hash(without_hash):
208	            raise _invalid_batch(f"record {index} hash does not match its contents")
209	        expected_prev = digest
210	
211	    expected_next = expected_seq if records else data[AFTER]
212	    if data[NEXT] != expected_next:
213	        raise _invalid_batch("next must be the last record seq, or after when empty")
214	
215	    # The bytes must be the exact canonical compact encoding export_batch
216	    # produces: no whitespace, no non-canonical escapes, fixed key order.
217	    if _compact(data) + b"\n" != batch:
218	        raise _invalid_batch("encoding is not the canonical compact form")
219	    return data
220	
221	
222	def _restore_log(path: str, existed: bool, size: int) -> None:
223	    """Best-effort rollback of a failed append.
224	
225	    Append-mode writes only ever extend the file, so truncating back to
226	    the pre-call size restores the exact prior bytes; a file the failed
227	    call newly created is unlinked again.  Rollback errors are swallowed
228	    so the original :class:`OSError` propagates unchanged.
229	    """
230	    try:
231	        if existed:
232	            with open(path, "r+b") as handle:
233	                handle.truncate(size)
234	                handle.flush()
235	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
236	        else:
237	            os.unlink(path)
238	    except OSError:
239	        pass
240	
241	
242	def import_batch(path: str, batch: bytes) -> dict:
243	    """Validate a replication batch and append its suffix to the local log.
244	
245	    See the module docstring for the byte contract.  A ``path`` that is not
246	    a str or a ``batch`` that is not bytes raises :class:`TypeError`; any
247	    contract violation raises :class:`ValueError`.  The local log is read
248	    solely through :func:`audit.read`, and a corrupt log or filesystem
249	    error propagates as :class:`~offline_coordination.audit.
250	    CorruptAuditError` or :class:`OSError`.  Any failure leaves the log
251	    byte-identical to its pre-call state (still missing when it was
252	    missing).
253	    """
254	    if not isinstance(path, str):
255	        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
256	    if not isinstance(batch, bytes):
257	        raise TypeError("batch must be bytes")
258	
259	    data = _parse_batch(batch)
260	    after = data[AFTER]
261	    batch_records = data[RECORDS]
262	
263	    local_records = audit.read(path)
264	    last_seq = local_records[-1][audit.SEQ] if local_records else 0
265	
266	    if after > last_seq:
267	        return {NEED: [last_seq + 1, after], NEXT: last_seq, STATUS: STATUS_MISSING}
268	
269	    # Records with seq <= last_seq must already exist locally and match the
270	    # batch record field by field; everything past last_seq is appended.
271	    suffix: list[dict] = []
272	    for record in batch_records:
273	        seq = record[audit.SEQ]
274	        if seq <= last_seq:
275	            local = local_records[seq - 1]
276	            if any(record[key] != local[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS):
277	                raise _invalid_batch(
278	                    f"record {seq} conflicts with the local record of the same seq"
279	                )
280	        else:
281	            if seq != last_seq + 1 + len(suffix):
282	                raise _invalid_batch("records past the local last seq must be contiguous")
283	            suffix.append(record)
284	
285	    if not suffix:
286	        return {NEED: None, NEXT: max(last_seq, data[NEXT]), STATUS: STATUS_DUPLICATE}
287	
288	    # The first appended record must chain onto the local log's last hash
289	    # (or the zero hash for an empty log).
290	    local_last_hash = local_records[-1][audit.HASH] if local_records else audit._ZERO_HASH
291	    if suffix[0][audit.PREV] != local_last_hash:
292	        raise _invalid_batch(
293	            "first new record prev must match the local last record hash"
294	        )
295	
296	    lines = b"".join(
297	        audit._encode_line({key: record[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS})
298	        for record in suffix
299	    )
300	    existed = os.path.exists(path)
301	    original_size = os.path.getsize(path) if existed else 0
302	    dir_fd: int | None = None
303	    try:
304	        with open(path, "ab") as handle:
305	            handle.write(lines)
306	            handle.flush()
307	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
308	        if not existed:
309	            dir_fd = os.open(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), os.O_RDONLY)
310	            os.fsync(dir_fd)
311	    except OSError:
312	        _restore_log(path, existed, original_size)
313	        raise
314	    finally:
315	        if dir_fd is not None:
316	            os.close(dir_fd)
317	
318	    return {NEED: None, NEXT: max(last_seq, data[NEXT]), STATUS: STATUS_APPLIED}

present locally must match field by field (a mismatch raises
:class:`ValueError`); the matching prefix is skipped idempotently and
only the contiguous suffix past ``L`` is appended, linked to the local
last hash.  ``need`` is then ``None``, ``next`` is ``max(L, batch.next)``
and ``status`` is ``"applied"`` when records were appended, else
``"duplicate"``.  Any failure leaves the log untouched.

Batch records are checked only against the byte contract: canonical
encoding, key order, the seq/prev/hash chain and the stored values.
Value-domain rules enforced by :func:`audit.append` on event input (the
kind enum, non-empty string fields) are *not* re-enforced here, so every
log :func:`audit.read` accepts round-trips through
:func:`export_batch`/:func:`import_batch`.  The append itself is atomic:
when the write, flush or fsync step raises :class:`OSError` the error
propagates unchanged and the log is left byte-identical to its pre-call
state (still missing when it was missing).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import re

from offline_coordination import audit

AFTER = "after"
COMPLETE = "complete"
NEED = "need"
NEXT = "next"
RECORDS = "records"
STATUS = "status"
VERSION = "version"

STATUS_MISSING = "missing"
STATUS_APPLIED = "applied"
STATUS_DUPLICATE = "duplicate"

_BATCH_KEYS = (AFTER, COMPLETE, NEXT, RECORDS, VERSION)
_RESULT_KEYS = (NEED, NEXT, STATUS)
_RECORD_KEYS = (
    audit.DETAIL,
    audit.HASH,
    audit.KIND,
    audit.PREV,
    audit.SEQ,
    audit.SOURCE,
)
_BATCH_VERSION = 1
_MIN_LIMIT = 1
_MAX_LIMIT = 1000
_HEX64 = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{64}")


def export_batch(path: str, after: int = 0, limit: int = 100) -> bytes:
    """Return one replication batch of audit records as UTF-8 JSON bytes.

    Selects the first ``limit`` records whose ``seq`` is greater than
    ``after``.  ``after`` must not exceed the log's last seq (an empty or
    missing log has last seq 0); otherwise :class:`ValueError` is raised.

    Type violations raise :class:`TypeError` (``bool`` is not accepted as
    an int); ``after < 0`` or a ``limit`` outside ``[1, 1000]`` raises
    :class:`ValueError`.  A corrupt log raises
    :class:`~offline_coordination.audit.CorruptAuditError` and filesystem
    errors propagate as :class:`OSError`.  The log is never modified.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
    if isinstance(after, bool) or not isinstance(after, int):
        raise TypeError("after must be an int")
    if isinstance(limit, bool) or not isinstance(limit, int):
        raise TypeError("limit must be an int")
    if after < 0:
        raise ValueError("after must be >= 0")
    if limit < _MIN_LIMIT or limit > _MAX_LIMIT:
        raise ValueError("limit must be in [1, 1000]")

    all_records = audit.read(path)
    last_seq = all_records[-1][audit.SEQ] if all_records else 0
    if after > last_seq:
        raise ValueError("after must not exceed the last audit seq")

    selected = [record for record in all_records if record[audit.SEQ] > after]
    selected = selected[:limit]
    batch_records = [
        {key: record[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS} for record in selected
    ]

    next_seq = batch_records[-1][audit.SEQ] if batch_records else after
    batch = {
        AFTER: after,
        COMPLETE: next_seq == last_seq,
        NEXT: next_seq,
        RECORDS: batch_records,
        VERSION: _BATCH_VERSION,
    }
    ordered = {key: batch[key] for key in _BATCH_KEYS}
    text = json.dumps(ordered, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
    return text.encode("utf-8")


def _invalid_batch(message: str) -> ValueError:
    return ValueError(f"invalid replication batch: {message}")


def _compact(obj: object) -> bytes:
    return json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")


def _parse_batch(batch: bytes) -> dict:
    """Validate a batch against the export byte contract and decode it."""
    if not batch.endswith(b"\n") or batch.endswith(b"\n\n"):
        raise _invalid_batch("must be a single JSON object terminated by one LF")
    try:
        data = json.loads(batch[:-1].decode("utf-8"))
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
        raise _invalid_batch("is not valid UTF-8 JSON") from exc

    if not isinstance(data, dict) or tuple(data.keys()) != _BATCH_KEYS:
        raise _invalid_batch(
            "top-level object must have exactly the keys "
            "'after', 'complete', 'next', 'records', 'version' in order"
        )
    version = data[VERSION]
    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int) or version != _BATCH_VERSION:
        raise _invalid_batch("version must be the integer 1")
    for key in (AFTER, NEXT):
        if isinstance(data[key], bool) or not isinstance(data[key], int):
            raise _invalid_batch(f"{key} must be an int")
        if data[key] < 0:
            raise _invalid_batch(f"{key} must be >= 0")
    if not isinstance(data[COMPLETE], bool):
        raise _invalid_batch("complete must be a bool")
    records = data[RECORDS]
    if not isinstance(records, list):
        raise _invalid_batch("records must be a list")
    if len(records) > _MAX_LIMIT:
        raise _invalid_batch("records must contain at most 1000 items")
    if not records and not data[COMPLETE]:
        raise _invalid_batch("empty records require complete to be true")

    expected_seq = data[AFTER]
    expected_prev = audit._ZERO_HASH if data[AFTER] == 0 else None
    for index, record in enumerate(records):
        if not isinstance(record, dict) or tuple(record.keys()) != _RECORD_KEYS:
            raise _invalid_batch(
                f"record {index} must have exactly the keys "
                "'detail', 'hash', 'kind', 'prev', 'seq', 'source' in order"
            )
        # Only the byte contract is enforced here: key order, the
        # seq/prev/hash chain and the stored values.  Value-domain rules
        # (non-empty fields, the kind enum) belong to audit.append's event
        # input, so records from any log audit.read accepts stay importable.
        prev = record[audit.PREV]
        digest = record[audit.HASH]
        if expected_prev is not None:
            if prev != expected_prev:
                raise _invalid_batch(
                    f"record {index} prev does not match the previous record hash"
                )
        elif not isinstance(prev, str) or not _HEX64.fullmatch(prev):
            # The first record's prev refers to the exporter's log and
            # cannot be checked against local state; require hash shape.
            raise _invalid_batch(f"record {index} prev must be 64 lowercase hex chars")
        seq = record[audit.SEQ]
        if isinstance(seq, bool) or not isinstance(seq, int):
            raise _invalid_batch(f"record {index} seq must be an int")
        expected_seq += 1
        if seq != expected_seq:
            raise _invalid_batch(
                f"record {index} seq is {seq}, expected {expected_seq}"
            )
        without_hash = {
            audit.DETAIL: record[audit.DETAIL],
            audit.KIND: record[audit.KIND],
            audit.PREV: prev,
            audit.SEQ: seq,
            audit.SOURCE: record[audit.SOURCE],
        }
        if digest != audit._record_hash(without_hash):
            raise _invalid_batch(f"record {index} hash does not match its contents")
        expected_prev = digest

    expected_next = expected_seq if records else data[AFTER]
    if data[NEXT] != expected_next:
        raise _invalid_batch("next must be the last record seq, or after when empty")

    # The bytes must be the exact canonical compact encoding export_batch
    # produces: no whitespace, no non-canonical escapes, fixed key order.
    if _compact(data) + b"\n" != batch:
        raise _invalid_batch("encoding is not the canonical compact form")
    return data


def _restore_log(path: str, existed: bool, size: int) -> None:
    """Best-effort rollback of a failed append.

    Append-mode writes only ever extend the file, so truncating back to
    the pre-call size restores the exact prior bytes; a file the failed
    call newly created is unlinked again.  Rollback errors are swallowed
    so the original :class:`OSError` propagates unchanged.
    """
    try:
        if existed:
            with open(path, "r+b") as handle:
                handle.truncate(size)
                handle.flush()
                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        else:
            os.unlink(path)
    except OSError:
        pass


def import_batch(path: str, batch: bytes) -> dict:
    """Validate a replication batch and append its suffix to the local log.

    See the module docstring for the byte contract.  A ``path`` that is not
    a str or a ``batch`` that is not bytes raises :class:`TypeError`; any
    contract violation raises :class:`ValueError`.  The local log is read
    solely through :func:`audit.read`, and a corrupt log or filesystem
    error propagates as :class:`~offline_coordination.audit.
    CorruptAuditError` or :class:`OSError`.  Any failure leaves the log
    byte-identical to its pre-call state (still missing when it was
    missing).
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
    if not isinstance(batch, bytes):
        raise TypeError("batch must be bytes")

    data = _parse_batch(batch)
    after = data[AFTER]
    batch_records = data[RECORDS]

    local_records = audit.read(path)
    last_seq = local_records[-1][audit.SEQ] if local_records else 0

    if after > last_seq:
        return {NEED: [last_seq + 1, after], NEXT: last_seq, STATUS: STATUS_MISSING}

    # Records with seq <= last_seq must already exist locally and match the
    # batch record field by field; everything past last_seq is appended.
    suffix: list[dict] = []
    for record in batch_records:
        seq = record[audit.SEQ]
        if seq <= last_seq:
            local = local_records[seq - 1]
            if any(record[key] != local[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS):
                raise _invalid_batch(
                    f"record {seq} conflicts with the local record of the same seq"
                )
        else:
            if seq != last_seq + 1 + len(suffix):
                raise _invalid_batch("records past the local last seq must be contiguous")
            suffix.append(record)

    if not suffix:
        return {NEED: None, NEXT: max(last_seq, data[NEXT]), STATUS: STATUS_DUPLICATE}

    # The first appended record must chain onto the local log's last hash
    # (or the zero hash for an empty log).
    local_last_hash = local_records[-1][audit.HASH] if local_records else audit._ZERO_HASH
    if suffix[0][audit.PREV] != local_last_hash:
        raise _invalid_batch(
            "first new record prev must match the local last record hash"
        )

    lines = b"".join(
        audit._encode_line({key: record[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS})
        for record in suffix
    )
    existed = os.path.exists(path)
    original_size = os.path.getsize(path) if existed else 0
    dir_fd: int | None = None
    try:
        with open(path, "ab") as handle:
            handle.write(lines)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        if not existed:
            dir_fd = os.open(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), os.O_RDONLY)
            os.fsync(dir_fd)
    except OSError:
        _restore_log(path, existed, original_size)
        raise
    finally:
        if dir_fd is not None:
            os.close(dir_fd)

    return {NEED: None, NEXT: max(last_seq, data[NEXT]), STATUS: STATUS_APPLIED}

"""Atomic state persistence for offline coordination.

A state (see :mod:`offline_coordination.merge`) is stored as UTF-8 JSON::

    json.dumps(state, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")) + "\\n"

with records kept as ``[value, deleted, clock, writer]`` lists.  Three paths
are used: the main file ``path``, a backup ``path + ".bak"`` holding the
previous most recent complete state, and a temporary file ``path + ".tmp"``
used for atomic replacement (and ignored when loading).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import errno
import json
import os
from typing import Any

from .merge import CLOCK, RECORDS, _validated_state


class CorruptStateError(ValueError):
    """State files exist, but none of them holds a valid state."""


def _serialize(clock: dict[str, int], records: dict[str, list[Any]]) -> bytes:
    state = {CLOCK: clock, RECORDS: records}
    text = (
        json.dumps(state, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
        + "\n"
    )
    return text.encode("utf-8")


def _decode_state(raw: bytes) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Decode and validate state bytes, returning a fresh deep-copied state."""
    data = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
    clock, records = _validated_state(data)
    return {CLOCK: clock, RECORDS: records}


_DECODE_FAILURES = (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError, ValueError)


def _read_valid_state(path: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Return the validated state stored at ``path``, or None if absent/corrupt."""
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None
    try:
        return _decode_state(raw)
    except _DECODE_FAILURES:
        return None


def _fsync_dir(path: str) -> None:
    """Fsync the directory containing ``path`` so a rename is durable.

    Any failure to open the directory or fsync it propagates as :class:`OSError`.
    """
    fd = os.open(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        os.fsync(fd)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def save_state(path: str, state: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Atomically persist ``state`` at ``path``, rotating the old state to backup.

    The state is validated with the same rules as
    :func:`offline_coordination.merge.merge_states` before anything touches
    the filesystem, so a rejected state leaves the existing files untouched.
    On success the main file holds the new state and the backup holds the
    previous most recent complete state (if there was one).  A crash at any
    point leaves at least one of the main and backup files readable.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
    clock, records = _validated_state(state)
    payload = _serialize(clock, records)

    main_path = path
    backup_path = path + ".bak"
    tmp_path = path + ".tmp"

    with open(tmp_path, "wb") as handle:
        handle.write(payload)
        handle.flush()
        os.fsync(handle.fileno())

    try:
        # Rotate only a complete state into the backup slot; a missing or
        # corrupt main file must not clobber a still-valid backup.
        if _read_valid_state(main_path) is not None:
            os.replace(main_path, backup_path)
        os.replace(tmp_path, main_path)
    except BaseException:
        try:
            os.unlink(tmp_path)
        except OSError:
            pass
        raise
    _fsync_dir(path)


def load_state(path: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Load the state stored at ``path``, falling back to the backup file.

    The temporary file is never consulted.  Returns a brand-new deep-copied
    state dict.  Raises :class:`FileNotFoundError` when neither file exists,
    :class:`CorruptStateError` when files exist but none decodes to a valid
    state, and re-raises any other :class:`OSError` from the filesystem.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise TypeError("path must be a str")

    saw_file = False
    for candidate in (path, path + ".bak"):
        try:
            with open(candidate, "rb") as handle:
                raw = handle.read()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            continue
        saw_file = True
        try:
            return _decode_state(raw)
        except _DECODE_FAILURES:
            continue
    if saw_file:
        raise CorruptStateError(f"no valid state found at {path!r}")
    raise FileNotFoundError(errno.ENOENT, "no state file found", path)

2	
3	The audit file is UTF-8 JSONL, one JSON object per line.  Each object has
4	the fixed key set and key order::
5	
6	    detail, hash, kind, prev, seq, source
7	
8	``seq`` starts at 1 and is contiguous; the first record's ``prev`` is 64
9	zero characters and every later ``prev`` equals the previous record's
10	``hash``.  ``hash`` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the compact UTF-8 JSON
11	encoding (no whitespace, non-ASCII preserved, no trailing newline) of the
12	record with the ``hash`` key itself removed and the remaining keys in the
13	order above.  Each complete record line is encoded the same way and
14	terminated by ``\\n``.
15	"""
16	
17	from __future__ import annotations
18	
19	import hashlib
20	import json
21	import os
22	from typing import Any
23	
24	DETAIL = "detail"
25	HASH = "hash"
26	KIND = "kind"
27	PREV = "prev"
28	SEQ = "seq"
29	SOURCE = "source"
30	
31	_EVENT_KEYS = (SOURCE, KIND, DETAIL)
32	_RECORD_KEYS = (DETAIL, HASH, KIND, PREV, SEQ, SOURCE)
33	_HASHED_KEYS = (DETAIL, KIND, PREV, SEQ, SOURCE)
34	_KINDS = ("local", "merge", "restore")
35	_ZERO_HASH = "0" * 64

38	class CorruptAuditError(ValueError):
39	    """The audit file exists but its contents are not a valid audit log."""
40	
41	
42	def _compact(obj: Any) -> bytes:
43	    # Same compact UTF-8 JSON rules used for state persistence in storage.py.
44	    return json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")

47	def _validated_event(event: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
48	    if not isinstance(event, dict):
49	        raise TypeError("event must be a dict")
50	    if set(event.keys()) != set(_EVENT_KEYS):
51	        raise ValueError(
52	            "event must contain exactly the keys 'source', 'kind' and 'detail'"
53	        )
54	    result: dict[str, str] = {}
55	    for key in _EVENT_KEYS:
56	        value = event[key]
57	        if not isinstance(value, str):
58	            raise TypeError(f"event {key} must be a str")
59	        if value == "":
60	            raise ValueError(f"event {key} must be non-empty")
61	        result[key] = value
62	    if result[KIND] not in _KINDS:
63	        raise ValueError("event kind must be one of 'local', 'merge' or 'restore'")
64	    return result

67	def _record_hash(record_without_hash: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
68	    ordered = {key: record_without_hash[key] for key in _HASHED_KEYS}
69	    return hashlib.sha256(_compact(ordered)).hexdigest()
70	
71	
72	def _encode_line(record: dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:
73	    ordered = {key: record[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS}
74	    return _compact(ordered) + b"\n"
75	
76	
77	def _parse_and_chain(raw: bytes) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
78	    """Validate every byte of an audit log and return its records.

"""Append-only hash-chained audit log for offline coordination.

The audit file is UTF-8 JSONL, one JSON object per line.  Each object has
the fixed key set and key order::

    detail, hash, kind, prev, seq, source

``seq`` starts at 1 and is contiguous; the first record's ``prev`` is 64
zero characters and every later ``prev`` equals the previous record's
``hash``.  ``hash`` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the compact UTF-8 JSON
encoding (no whitespace, non-ASCII preserved, no trailing newline) of the
record with the ``hash`` key itself removed and the remaining keys in the
order above.  Each complete record line is encoded the same way and
terminated by ``\\n``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
from typing import Any

DETAIL = "detail"
HASH = "hash"
KIND = "kind"
PREV = "prev"
SEQ = "seq"
SOURCE = "source"

_EVENT_KEYS = (SOURCE, KIND, DETAIL)
_RECORD_KEYS = (DETAIL, HASH, KIND, PREV, SEQ, SOURCE)
_HASHED_KEYS = (DETAIL, KIND, PREV, SEQ, SOURCE)
_KINDS = ("local", "merge", "restore")
_ZERO_HASH = "0" * 64


class CorruptAuditError(ValueError):
    """The audit file exists but its contents are not a valid audit log."""


def _compact(obj: Any) -> bytes:
    # Same compact UTF-8 JSON rules used for state persistence in storage.py.
    return json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")


def _validated_event(event: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
    if not isinstance(event, dict):
        raise TypeError("event must be a dict")
    if set(event.keys()) != set(_EVENT_KEYS):
        raise ValueError(
            "event must contain exactly the keys 'source', 'kind' and 'detail'"
        )
    result: dict[str, str] = {}
    for key in _EVENT_KEYS:
        value = event[key]
        if not isinstance(value, str):
            raise TypeError(f"event {key} must be a str")
        if value == "":
            raise ValueError(f"event {key} must be non-empty")
        result[key] = value
    if result[KIND] not in _KINDS:
        raise ValueError("event kind must be one of 'local', 'merge' or 'restore'")
    return result


def _record_hash(record_without_hash: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    ordered = {key: record_without_hash[key] for key in _HASHED_KEYS}
    return hashlib.sha256(_compact(ordered)).hexdigest()


def _encode_line(record: dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:
    ordered = {key: record[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS}
    return _compact(ordered) + b"\n"


def _parse_and_chain(raw: bytes) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Validate every byte of an audit log and return its records.

    Raises :class:`CorruptAuditError` for any UTF-8/JSON decoding failure,
    non-canonical byte encoding, wrong key set, seq/prev/hash chain break,
    or missing line terminator.  Value-domain rules (non-empty fields, the
    kind enum) are enforced on event input by :func:`append`.
    """
    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise CorruptAuditError("audit file is not valid UTF-8") from exc

    records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    expected_seq = 1
    expected_prev = _ZERO_HASH

    if text == "":
        return records
    # Every record, including the last one, must be newline-terminated; the
    # trailing empty segment is the expected terminator.  Interior empty
    # segments are blank lines and fail canonical re-encoding below.
    lines = text.split("\n")
    if lines[-1] != "":
        raise CorruptAuditError("the last audit line is not terminated by a newline")
    for line_no, line in enumerate(lines[:-1], start=1):
        line_bytes = line.encode("utf-8")
        try:
            data = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise CorruptAuditError(
                f"audit line {line_no} is not valid JSON"
            ) from exc
        if not isinstance(data, dict):
            raise CorruptAuditError(f"audit line {line_no} is not a JSON object")
        if set(data.keys()) != set(_RECORD_KEYS):
            raise CorruptAuditError(
                f"audit line {line_no} must contain exactly the keys "
                "detail, hash, kind, prev, seq, source"
            )
        detail = data[DETAIL]
        kind = data[KIND]
        prev = data[PREV]
        seq = data[SEQ]
        source = data[SOURCE]
        digest = data[HASH]
        # seq must be a genuine JSON integer (a bool would compare equal to
        # 0/1 and slip past the chain check in Python).
        if isinstance(seq, bool) or not isinstance(seq, int):
            raise CorruptAuditError(f"audit line {line_no} seq must be an int")
        if seq != expected_seq:
            raise CorruptAuditError(
                f"audit line {line_no} seq is {seq}, expected {expected_seq}"
            )
        if prev != expected_prev:
            raise CorruptAuditError(
                f"audit line {line_no} prev does not match the previous hash"
            )
        without_hash = {
            DETAIL: detail,
            KIND: kind,
            PREV: prev,
            SEQ: seq,
            SOURCE: source,
        }
        actual_hash = _record_hash(without_hash)
        if digest != actual_hash:
            raise CorruptAuditError(
                f"audit line {line_no} hash does not match its contents"
            )
        record = {key: None for key in _RECORD_KEYS}
        record[DETAIL] = detail
        record[KIND] = kind
        record[PREV] = prev
        record[SEQ] = seq
        record[SOURCE] = source
        record[HASH] = digest
        # The on-disk bytes must be the single canonical compact encoding:
        # this rejects stray whitespace, non-canonical escapes, and any key
        # order other than the fixed one.
        if _compact({key: record[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS}) != line_bytes:
            raise CorruptAuditError(
                f"audit line {line_no} is not canonically encoded"
            )
        records.append(record)
        expected_seq += 1
        expected_prev = digest

    return records


def _read_all_records(path: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return []
    return _parse_and_chain(raw)


def append(path: str, event: dict[str, str]) -> int:
    """Append one audit event to the log at ``path`` and return its seq.

    Every existing line is verified before anything is written, so a corrupt
    log is never extended.  The new line is flushed and fsynced; when the
    file is newly created its parent directory is fsynced as well.

    Type violations raise :class:`TypeError`; invalid event contents raise
    :class:`ValueError`; a corrupt log raises :class:`CorruptAuditError`;
    other filesystem errors propagate as :class:`OSError`.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
    event_fields = _validated_event(event)

    existed = os.path.exists(path)
    records = _read_all_records(path)
    seq = len(records) + 1
    prev = records[-1][HASH] if records else _ZERO_HASH

    without_hash = {
        DETAIL: event_fields[DETAIL],
        KIND: event_fields[KIND],
        PREV: prev,
        SEQ: seq,
        SOURCE: event_fields[SOURCE],
    }
    digest = _record_hash(without_hash)
    record = dict(without_hash)
    record[HASH] = digest
    line = _encode_line(record)

    with open(path, "ab") as handle:
        handle.write(line)
        handle.flush()
        os.fsync(handle.fileno())

    if not existed:
        fd = os.open(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), os.O_RDONLY)
        try:
            os.fsync(fd)
        finally:
            os.close(fd)

    return seq


def read(path: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Return all audit records at ``path`` as a fresh deep-copied list.

    A missing or empty file yields an empty list.  A corrupt log raises
    :class:`CorruptAuditError`; other filesystem errors propagate as
    :class:`OSError`.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
    return _read_all_records(path)

1	"""State merging for offline coordination.
2	
3	A state is a dict of the form::
4	
5	    {"clock": {node: count}, "records": {key: [value, deleted, clock, writer]}}
6	
7	``clock`` maps non-empty node names to non-negative integer counters.
8	Each record is a four-item list ``[value, deleted, clock, writer]`` where
9	``value`` is a str (always ``""`` for a deleted record), ``deleted`` is a
10	bool, ``clock`` is the record's vector clock (it must contain ``writer`` and
11	no component may exceed the outer state clock; missing nodes count as 0),
12	and ``writer`` is a non-empty str.
13	
14	See :func:`merge_states` for the reconciliation rules.
15	"""
16	
17	from __future__ import annotations
18	
19	from typing import Any
20	
21	CLOCK = "clock"
22	RECORDS = "records"
23	
24	
25	def _is_int(value: Any) -> bool:
26	    # bool is a subclass of int, but a counter must never be a bool.
27	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
28	
29	
30	def _is_nonempty_str(value: Any) -> bool:
31	    return isinstance(value, str) and value != ""

35	    clock: Any, *, where: str, bound: dict[str, int] | None = None
36	) -> dict[str, int]:
37	    """Validate a clock mapping and return a fresh dict copy.
38	
39	    When ``bound`` is given, every component must be <= the corresponding
40	    bound value; nodes absent from the bound are treated as 0.
41	    """
42	    if not isinstance(clock, dict):
43	        raise TypeError(f"{where} clock must be a dict")
44	    result: dict[str, int] = {}
45	    for node, count in clock.items():
46	        if not isinstance(node, str):
47	            raise TypeError(f"{where} clock node must be a str")
48	        if node == "":
49	            raise ValueError(f"{where} clock node must be non-empty")
50	        if not _is_int(count):
51	            raise TypeError(f"{where} clock count for {node!r} must be an int")
52	        if count < 0:
53	            raise ValueError(f"{where} clock count for {node!r} must be non-negative")
54	        result[node] = count
55	    if bound is not None:
56	        for node, count in result.items():
57	            limit = bound.get(node, 0)
58	            if count > limit:
59	                raise ValueError(
60	                    f"{where} clock count for {node!r} ({count}) exceeds the "
61	                    f"state clock ({limit})"
62	                )
63	    return result
64	
65	
66	def _validated_record(
67	    entry: Any, *, key: str, state_clock: dict[str, int]
68	) -> list[Any]:
69	    """Validate one record and return a fresh list with a copied clock."""
70	    where = f"record for key {key!r}"
71	    if not isinstance(entry, list):
72	        raise TypeError(f"{where} must be a list")
73	    if len(entry) != 4:
74	        raise ValueError(f"{where} must have exactly four items")
75	    value, deleted, clock, writer = entry
76	    if not isinstance(value, str):
77	        raise TypeError(f"{where} value must be a str")
78	    if not isinstance(deleted, bool):
79	        raise TypeError(f"{where} deleted flag must be a bool")
80	    if deleted and value != "":
81	        raise ValueError(f"{where} is deleted but its value is not empty")
82	    clock_copy = _validated_clock(clock, where=where, bound=state_clock)
83	    if not isinstance(writer, str):
84	        raise TypeError(f"{where} writer must be a str")
85	    if writer == "":
86	        raise ValueError(f"{where} writer must be non-empty")
87	    if writer not in clock_copy:
88	        raise ValueError(f"{where} writer {writer!r} is missing from its clock")
89	    return [value, deleted, clock_copy, writer]

92	def _validated_state(state: Any) -> tuple[dict[str, int], dict[str, list[Any]]]:
93	    """Validate a whole state and return fresh copies of its contents."""
94	    if not isinstance(state, dict):
95	        raise TypeError("state must be a dict")
96	    if set(state.keys()) != {CLOCK, RECORDS}:
97	        raise ValueError("state must contain exactly the keys 'clock' and 'records'")

113	    """True iff every component of winner is >= and at least one is >.

118	    return all(winner.get(node, 0) >= loser.get(node, 0) for node in nodes) and any(
119	        winner.get(node, 0) > loser.get(node, 0) for node in nodes

124	    value, deleted, clock, writer = record

155	    is behind contributes the closed interval ``[local + 1, prerequisite]``.

159	    for node in sorted(set(local_clock) | set(remote_clock)):
160	        prerequisite = remote_clock.get(node, 0) - (1 if node == writer else 0)

234	    * A record present on only one side is kept as-is.
235	    * Identical records are kept.
236	    * If one record's clock has every component >= the other's with at least
237	      one strictly greater, that record wins.
238	    * Otherwise the record with the larger
239	      ``(clock[writer], writer, deleted, value, tuple(sorted(clock.items())))``
240	      Python tuple wins.
241	
242	    Type violations raise :class:`TypeError`; all other constraint violations
243	    raise :class:`ValueError`.
244	    """
245	    left_clock, left_records = _validated_state(left)
246	    right_clock, right_records = _validated_state(right)
247	
248	    merged_clock: dict[str, int] = {}
249	    for node in set(left_clock) | set(right_clock):
250	        merged_clock[node] = max(left_clock.get(node, 0), right_clock.get(node, 0))
251	
252	    merged_records: dict[str, list[Any]] = {}
253	    for key in set(left_records) | set(right_records):
254	        left_record = left_records.get(key)
255	        right_record = right_records.get(key)
256	        if left_record is None:
257	            chosen = right_record
258	        elif right_record is None:
259	            chosen = left_record
260	        else:
261	            chosen = _resolve_record(left_record, right_record)
262	        value, deleted, record_clock, writer = chosen
263	        merged_records[key] = [value, deleted, dict(record_clock), writer]
264	
265	    return {CLOCK: merged_clock, RECORDS: merged_records}

5	are never read or written here.  Receipts are kept in an index stored as
6	UTF-8 compact JSON::

8	    {"items":[{"audit":...,"id":...,"state":...},...],"version":1}\\n

11	``version`` is always the integer 1.  ``items`` is an array of records
12	sorted ascending by ``id`` (ids are unique); each record carries the str
13	keys ``id``, ``state`` and ``audit`` and is canonically encoded with the
14	key order ``audit``, ``id``, ``state``.  Non-ASCII characters are preserved

18	violates any byte, structure, order or field rule is corrupt.

23	import json
24	import os
25	import re
26	from typing import Any

28	AUDIT = "audit"
29	ID = "id"
30	STATE = "state"
31	
32	ITEMS = "items"
33	VERSION = "version"

35	_RECEIPT_KEYS = (ID, STATE, AUDIT)
36	_RECORD_KEYS = (AUDIT, ID, STATE)
37	_INDEX_KEYS = (ITEMS, VERSION)
38	_INDEX_VERSION = 1

45	    """The receipt index exists but its bytes are not a valid index."""

49	    return isinstance(value, str) and _DIGEST_RE.fullmatch(value) is not None

52	def _validated_receipt(receipt: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
53	    """Validate one receipt and return a fresh dict in record key order."""
54	    if not isinstance(receipt, dict):
55	        raise TypeError("receipt must be a dict")
56	    if set(receipt.keys()) != set(_RECEIPT_KEYS):
57	        raise ValueError(

59	        )

76	        for record in records

83	def _parse_index(raw: bytes) -> list[dict[str, str]]:

96	    try:
97	        data = json.loads(text)
98	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
99	        raise CorruptReceiptError("receipt index is not valid JSON") from exc

101	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
102	        raise CorruptReceiptError("receipt index must be a JSON object")
103	    if set(data.keys()) != set(_INDEX_KEYS):
104	        raise CorruptReceiptError(

106	        )
107	    if list(data.keys()) != list(_INDEX_KEYS):

113	    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int) or version != 1:

116	    if not isinstance(raw_items, list):
117	        raise CorruptReceiptError("receipt index items must be an array")

120	    for position, item in enumerate(raw_items):
121	        where = f"receipt index item {position}"
122	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
123	            raise CorruptReceiptError(f"{where} must be a JSON object")
124	        if set(item.keys()) != set(_RECORD_KEYS):
125	            raise CorruptReceiptError(

127	            )
128	        if list(item.keys()) != list(_RECORD_KEYS):
129	            raise CorruptReceiptError(
130	                f"{where} keys must be in the order 'audit', 'id', 'state'"
131	            )

171	def _atomic_write(path: str, payload: bytes) -> None:
172	    tmp_path = path + ".tmp"
173	    with open(tmp_path, "wb") as handle:
174	        handle.write(payload)
175	        handle.flush()
176	        os.fsync(handle.fileno())
177	    try:
178	        os.replace(tmp_path, path)
179	    except BaseException:
180	        try:
181	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
182	        except OSError:
183	            pass
184	        raise
185	    fd = os.open(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), os.O_RDONLY)
186	    try:
187	        os.fsync(fd)

192	def put(path: str, receipt: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:

194	
195	    A new id is added and the index is atomically replaced.  Putting the
196	    same id with identical state and audit digests is idempotent: a fresh
197	    dict is returned without touching the file bytes.  The same id with
198	    different digests raises :class:`ValueError` and leaves the file
199	    unchanged.  The returned dict always has the key order
200	    ``audit``, ``id``, ``state``.
201	
202	    Type violations raise :class:`TypeError`; a bad key set, id or digest
203	    format raises :class:`ValueError`; a corrupt index raises
204	    :class:`CorruptReceiptError`; other filesystem errors propagate as
205	    :class:`OSError`.
206	    """
207	    if not isinstance(path, str):
208	        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
209	    record = _validated_receipt(receipt)
210	
211	    records = _read_index(path)
212	    for existing in records:
213	        if existing[ID] == record[ID]:
214	            if (
215	                existing[STATE] != record[STATE]
216	                or existing[AUDIT] != record[AUDIT]
217	            ):
218	                raise ValueError(
219	                    f"receipt id {record[ID]!r} is already bound to a "
220	                    "different state or audit record"
221	                )
222	            # Idempotent replay: brand-new copy, no filesystem change.
223	            return dict(record)
224	
225	    records.append(record)
226	    records.sort(key=lambda entry: entry[ID])
227	    _atomic_write(path, _serialize_index(records))
228	    return dict(record)
229	
230	
231	def get(path: str, id: str) -> dict[str, str] | None:
232	    """Return a fresh copy of the receipt stored under ``id``, or None.
233	
234	    A missing index file or an index without that id yields ``None``.
235	    Type violations raise :class:`TypeError`; a malformed ``id`` raises
236	    :class:`ValueError`; a corrupt index raises
237	    :class:`CorruptReceiptError`; other filesystem errors propagate as
238	    :class:`OSError`.
239	    """
240	    if not isinstance(path, str):
241	        raise TypeError("path must be a str")

243	        raise TypeError("id must be a str")
244	    if _ID_RE.fullmatch(id) is None:
245	        raise ValueError("id must match [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}")
246	
247	    for record in _read_index(path):
248	        if record[ID] == id:
249	            return dict(record)

1	"""Replayable commit checkpoints for offline coordination.
2	
3	A checkpoint names an ``id``, the two 64-char lowercase hex digests of the
4	state and audit bytes it binds, and the ``stage`` the commit has reached.
5	Stages advance in the fixed order::
6	
7	    prepared -> state -> audit -> committed
8	
9	Checkpoints are kept in an index stored as UTF-8 compact JSON::
10	
11	    {"items":[{"audit":...,"id":...,"stage":...,"state":...},...],"version":1}\\n
12	
13	The top-level keys are fixed in the order ``items`` then ``version`` and
14	``version`` is always the integer 1.  ``items`` is an array of records
15	sorted ascending by ``id`` (ids are unique); each record carries the str
16	keys ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage`` and ``state`` in that order.  Non-ASCII
17	characters are preserved unescaped and the file ends with exactly one
18	``\\n``.
19	
20	A missing index file stands for an empty index.  An existing file is
21	corrupt unless it is one compact UTF-8 JSON encoding of a valid index:
22	no stray whitespace or non-canonical escapes and exactly one trailing
23	``\\n``.  The object *key order* carries no meaning, however, so an
24	otherwise identical compact encoding with the top-level or record keys
25	permuted is accepted as equivalent; files written by this module always
26	use the canonical key order described above.
27	
28	A brand-new id may only be recorded at the ``prepared`` stage.  Replaying
29	the same id with identical digests at the same stage is idempotent and
30	leaves the file bytes untouched; the stage may then advance one step at a
31	time, each advance replacing the file atomically.  Changed digests, a
32	stage regression or a skipped stage are rejected and never touch the file.
33	
34	:func:`resume` drives a single recovery step.  Its request carries only
35	the ``id``, ``state`` and ``audit`` digests and ``observed`` names the
36	stage the caller believes it has reached (``None`` for a fresh resume).
37	A new id is only accepted with ``observed=None`` and starts at
38	``prepared``.  For an existing id with identical digests, ``observed``
39	of ``None`` or the current stage only queries the index (leaving the
40	file bytes untouched), while the adjacent next stage advances it once;
41	a regression, a skipped stage or an illegal value is rejected without
42	touching the file.  The return value names the next action for the
43	processed stage: ``persist_state`` after ``prepared``,
44	``append_audit`` after ``state``, ``bind_receipt`` after ``audit`` and
45	``done`` after ``committed``.
46	
47	:func:`commit` drives a whole commit to completion.  Its ``paths`` map
48	names the ``checkpoint``, ``state``, ``audit`` and ``receipt`` files and
49	its request carries the ``id``, the full merge ``state`` and one audit
50	``event``.  The state digest is the SHA-256 of the canonical state bytes
51	storage writes; the audit digest is the hash of the one appended audit
52	record.  A first commit persists the state, appends exactly one event,
53	binds a receipt for the id and both digests, and advances the checkpoint
54	through the stages in order.  Replaying the same call -- after an
55	interruption or once committed -- deterministically resumes at the
56	recorded stage and performs every remaining side effect at most once,
57	returning the same ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage`` (``committed``) and
58	``state`` dict.  A digest conflict, or a checkpoint stage whose
59	artifacts do not match it, raises :class:`ValueError` and leaves the
60	files unchanged.
61	
62	:func:`inspect` is a strictly read-only counterpart taking only the
63	``paths`` map.  A missing checkpoint index yields an empty list; every
64	existing checkpoint is reported with its ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage``
65	and ``state`` values plus a ``status`` of ``recoverable``,
66	``committed`` or ``conflict`` derived from the state bytes, the audit
67	chain and any bound receipt.  Neither :func:`inspect` nor
68	:func:`commit` ever treats an existing-but-unreadable state as a mere

246	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
247	            raise CorruptTransactionError(f"{where} must be a JSON object")
248	        if set(item.keys()) != set(_RECORD_KEYS):
249	            raise CorruptTransactionError(
250	                f"{where} must contain exactly the keys 'audit', 'id', 'stage' "
251	                "and 'state'"
252	            )
253	        audit_digest = item[AUDIT]
254	        record_id = item[ID]
255	        stage = item[STAGE]
256	        state_digest = item[STATE]
257	        if not isinstance(record_id, str) or _ID_RE.fullmatch(record_id) is None:
258	            raise CorruptTransactionError(f"{where} has an invalid id")
259	        if not isinstance(stage, str) or stage not in _STAGE_RANK:
260	            raise CorruptTransactionError(f"{where} has an invalid stage")
261	        if not isinstance(state_digest, str) or not _is_digest(state_digest):
262	            raise CorruptTransactionError(
263	                f"{where} state must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
264	            )
265	        if not isinstance(audit_digest, str) or not _is_digest(audit_digest):
266	            raise CorruptTransactionError(
267	                f"{where} audit must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
268	            )
269	        records.append(
270	            {AUDIT: audit_digest, ID: record_id, STAGE: stage, STATE: state_digest}
271	        )
272	
273	    ids = [record[ID] for record in records]
274	    if any(left >= right for left, right in zip(ids, ids[1:])):
275	        raise CorruptTransactionError(
276	            "checkpoint index ids must be unique and sorted ascending"
277	        )
278	
279	    # Reject stray whitespace, non-canonical escapes, duplicate keys and
280	    # any encoding that is not a single compact form of the validated
281	    # structure.  Re-serialising the parsed object while preserving its
282	    # parsed key order tolerates permuted object keys (a semantically
283	    # equivalent compact index) while still rejecting every other
284	    # byte-level deviation; writes always use the canonical key order of
285	    # _serialize_index.
286	    if not raw.endswith(b"\n") or raw.endswith(b"\n\n"):
287	        raise CorruptTransactionError(
288	            "checkpoint index must end with exactly one newline"
289	        )
290	    compact = json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
291	    if compact != text[:-1]:
292	        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index is not canonically encoded")
293	    return records

296	def _read_index(path: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
297	    try:
298	        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
299	            raw = handle.read()
300	    except FileNotFoundError:
301	        return []
302	    return _parse_index(raw)

305	def _atomic_write(path: str, payload: bytes) -> None:
306	    tmp_path = path + ".tmp"
307	    with open(tmp_path, "wb") as handle:
308	        handle.write(payload)
309	        handle.flush()
310	        os.fsync(handle.fileno())
311	    try:
312	        os.replace(tmp_path, path)
313	    except BaseException:
314	        try:
315	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
316	        except OSError:
317	            pass
318	        raise
319	    fd = os.open(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), os.O_RDONLY)
320	    try:
321	        os.fsync(fd)
322	    finally:
323	        os.close(fd)

326	def _apply(
327	    path: str, records: list[dict[str, str]], record: dict[str, str]
328	) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
329	    """Apply ``record`` to ``records`` and return the resulting record list."""
330	    for position, existing in enumerate(records):
331	        if existing[ID] != record[ID]:
332	            continue
333	        if (
334	            existing[STATE] != record[STATE]
335	            or existing[AUDIT] != record[AUDIT]
336	        ):
337	            raise ValueError(
338	                f"checkpoint id {record[ID]!r} is already bound to different "
339	                "state or audit digests"
340	            )
341	        old_rank = _STAGE_RANK[existing[STAGE]]
342	        new_rank = _STAGE_RANK[record[STAGE]]
343	        if new_rank == old_rank:
344	            # Idempotent replay: no filesystem change.
345	            return records
346	        if new_rank < old_rank:
347	            raise ValueError(
348	                f"checkpoint id {record[ID]!r} cannot regress from stage "
349	                f"{existing[STAGE]!r} to {record[STAGE]!r}"
350	            )
351	        if new_rank > old_rank + 1:
352	            raise ValueError(
353	                f"checkpoint id {record[ID]!r} cannot skip from stage "
354	                f"{existing[STAGE]!r} to {record[STAGE]!r}"
355	            )
356	        updated = list(records)
357	        updated[position] = record
358	        _atomic_write(path, _serialize_index(updated))
359	        return updated
360	
361	    if record[STAGE] != PREPARED:
362	        raise ValueError("a new checkpoint id must start at the 'prepared' stage")
363	    updated = sorted(records + [record], key=lambda entry: entry[ID])
364	    _atomic_write(path, _serialize_index(updated))
365	    return updated

368	def checkpoint(
369	    path: str, request: dict[str, str] | None = None
370	) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
371	    """Record or query a replayable commit checkpoint at ``path``.
372	
373	    With ``request=None`` this is a pure query returning every checkpoint.
374	    Otherwise ``request`` must contain exactly the str keys ``id``,
375	    ``state``, ``audit`` and ``stage``: ``id`` matches
376	    ``[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}``, ``state`` and ``audit`` are 64 lowercase hex
377	    characters, and ``stage`` is one of ``prepared``, ``state``, ``audit``
378	    or ``committed``.
379	
380	    A new id is inserted at ``prepared``; an existing id with identical
381	    digests replays idempotently at the same stage or advances one adjacent
382	    stage.  Changed digests, a stage regression or a skipped stage raise
383	    :class:`ValueError` and leave the file unchanged.  In every case a
384	    brand-new list sorted ascending by ``id`` is returned, each element a
385	    fresh dict with the key order ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage``, ``state``.
386	
387	    Type violations raise :class:`TypeError`; a bad key set, field format
388	    or stage migration raises :class:`ValueError`; a corrupt index raises
389	    :class:`CorruptTransactionError`; other filesystem errors propagate as
390	    :class:`OSError`.
391	    """
392	    if not isinstance(path, str):
393	        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
394	
395	    record = _validated_request(request) if request is not None else None
396	    records = _read_index(path)
397	    if record is not None:
398	        records = _apply(path, records, record)
399	
400	    return [
401	        {
402	            AUDIT: record[AUDIT],
403	            ID: record[ID],
404	            STAGE: record[STAGE],
405	            STATE: record[STATE],
406	        }
407	        for record in records
408	    ]

411	def resume(
412	    path: str, request: dict[str, str], observed: str | None = None
413	) -> str:
414	    """Recover one commit step at ``path`` and return the next action.
415	
416	    ``request`` must contain exactly the str keys ``id``, ``state`` and
417	    ``audit`` in the same format as the matching :func:`checkpoint`
418	    fields.  ``observed`` must be ``None`` or one of the stages
419	    ``prepared``, ``state``, ``audit`` or ``committed``; it names the
420	    stage the caller has observed for the id.
421	
422	    A new id is only accepted with ``observed=None`` and is recorded at
423	    the ``prepared`` stage.  An existing id must be bound to the same
424	    ``state`` and ``audit`` digests; with ``observed=None`` or the
425	    current stage the call is a pure query and leaves the file bytes
426	    untouched, while ``observed`` naming the adjacent next stage
427	    advances the checkpoint exactly once.  A stage regression, a skipped
428	    stage or an illegal ``observed`` value raise :class:`ValueError` and
429	    leave the file unchanged.
430	
431	    The return value is the next action for the processed stage:
432	    ``persist_state`` for ``prepared``, ``append_audit`` for ``state``,
433	    ``bind_receipt`` for ``audit`` and ``done`` for ``committed``.
434	
435	    A non-str ``observed`` other than ``None`` raises :class:`TypeError`;
436	    the remaining type and value rules, :class:`CorruptTransactionError`
437	    and :class:`OSError` propagation match :func:`checkpoint`.
438	    """
439	    if not isinstance(path, str):
440	        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
441	
442	    requested = _validated_resume_request(request)
443	    if observed is not None:
444	        if not isinstance(observed, str):
445	            raise TypeError(
446	                "observed must be None or one of 'prepared', 'state', "
447	                "'audit' or 'committed'"
448	            )
449	        if observed not in _STAGE_RANK:
450	            raise ValueError(
451	                "observed must be None or one of 'prepared', 'state', "
452	                "'audit' or 'committed'"
453	            )
454	
455	    records = _read_index(path)
456	    existing = next(
457	        (record for record in records if record[ID] == requested[ID]), None
458	    )
459	
460	    if existing is None:
461	        if observed is not None:
462	            raise ValueError(
463	                f"checkpoint id {requested[ID]!r} is new and may only be "
464	                "resumed with observed=None"
465	            )
466	        record = {
467	            AUDIT: requested[AUDIT],
468	            ID: requested[ID],
469	            STAGE: PREPARED,
470	            STATE: requested[STATE],
471	        }
472	        _apply(path, records, record)
473	        return _NEXT_ACTIONS[PREPARED]
474	
475	    if (
476	        existing[STATE] != requested[STATE]
477	        or existing[AUDIT] != requested[AUDIT]
478	    ):
479	        raise ValueError(
480	            f"checkpoint id {requested[ID]!r} is already bound to different "
481	            "state or audit digests"
482	        )
483	
484	    current_stage = existing[STAGE]
485	    if observed is None or observed == current_stage:
486	        # Pure query: no filesystem change.
487	        processed_stage = current_stage
488	    else:
489	        current_rank = _STAGE_RANK[current_stage]
490	        observed_rank = _STAGE_RANK[observed]
491	        if observed_rank < current_rank:
492	            raise ValueError(
493	                f"checkpoint id {requested[ID]!r} cannot regress from stage "
494	                f"{current_stage!r} to {observed!r}"
495	            )
496	        if observed_rank > current_rank + 1:
497	            raise ValueError(
498	                f"checkpoint id {requested[ID]!r} cannot skip from stage "
499	                f"{current_stage!r} to {observed!r}"
500	            )
501	        record = {
502	            AUDIT: requested[AUDIT],
503	            ID: requested[ID],
504	            STAGE: observed,
505	            STATE: requested[STATE],
506	        }
507	        _apply(path, records, record)
508	        processed_stage = observed
509	
510	    return _NEXT_ACTIONS[processed_stage]
511

522	    if not isinstance(paths, dict):

536	    paths: Any, request: Any
537	) -> tuple[dict[str, str], str, dict[str, Any], dict[str, str], bytes]:
538	    """Validate ``paths`` and a commit ``request`` before any file access.
539	
540	    Returns the path map, id, the caller's state, a fresh validated event
541	    dict and the canonical state bytes.  The state is checked against the
542	    merge state contract and the event against the audit event contract,
543	    so their type/value errors propagate unchanged in kind.
544	    """
545	    path_map = _validated_paths(paths)
546	    if not isinstance(request, dict):
547	        raise TypeError("request must be a dict")
548	    if set(request.keys()) != set(_COMMIT_KEYS):
549	        raise ValueError(
550	            "request must contain exactly the keys 'id', 'state' and 'event'"

558	    payload = _state_payload(request[STATE])
559	    event = _audit._validated_event(request[_EVENT])

564	def _planned_audit_digest(
565	    audit_records: list[dict[str, Any]], event: dict[str, str]
566	) -> str:
567	    """Hash the audit record the next :func:`audit.append` would write.
568	
569	    Deterministic from the log's current tail: its seq is one past the
570	    last record and its prev is the last record's hash (or the zero hash
571	    for an empty log).
572	    """
573	    seq = len(audit_records) + 1
574	    prev = audit_records[-1][_audit.HASH] if audit_records else _audit._ZERO_HASH
575	    without_hash = {
576	        _audit.DETAIL: event[_audit.DETAIL],
577	        _audit.KIND: event[_audit.KIND],
578	        _audit.PREV: prev,
579	        _audit.SEQ: seq,
580	        _audit.SOURCE: event[_audit.SOURCE],
581	    }
582	    return _audit._record_hash(without_hash)

659	def _inspect_status(
660	    stage: str,
661	    state_matches: bool,
662	    audit_ok: bool,
663	    receipt: dict[str, str] | None,
664	    state_digest: str,
665	    audit_digest: str,
666	) -> str:
667	    """Classify one checkpoint from its stage and the S/A/R0/R1 facts.
668	
669	    ``S`` is ``state_matches`` (the main state file's canonical bytes hash
670	    to the state digest), ``A`` is ``audit_ok`` (a valid audit chain
671	    carries the audit digest), ``R0`` means no receipt is bound under the
672	    id and ``R1`` means that receipt binds exactly both digests.
673	    ``prepared`` with ``not A and R0``, ``state`` with ``S and R0`` and
674	    ``audit`` with ``S and A and (R0 or R1)`` are recoverable;
675	    ``committed`` with ``S and A and R1`` is committed; everything else
676	    is a conflict.
677	    """
678	    r0 = receipt is None
679	    r1 = (
680	        receipt is not None
681	        and receipt[STATE] == state_digest
682	        and receipt[AUDIT] == audit_digest
683	    )
684	    if stage == PREPARED:
685	        if not audit_ok and r0:
686	            return RECOVERABLE
687	    elif stage == STAGE_STATE:
688	        if state_matches and r0:
689	            return RECOVERABLE
690	    elif stage == STAGE_AUDIT:
691	        if state_matches and audit_ok and (r0 or r1):
692	            return RECOVERABLE
693	    else:  # COMMITTED
694	        if state_matches and audit_ok and r1:
695	            return COMMITTED
696	    return CONFLICT

699	def inspect(paths: dict[str, str]) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
700	    """Read-only inspection of every checkpoint against its bound artifacts.
701	
702	    ``paths`` must contain exactly the str keys ``checkpoint``, ``state``,
703	    ``audit`` and ``receipt``, naming the checkpoint index, the main state
704	    file (its ``path + ".bak"`` backup is consulted for corruption
705	    detection, exactly as :func:`storage.load_state` does), the audit log
706	    and the receipt index.
707	
708	    A missing checkpoint index yields ``[]`` (no other artifact is read in
709	    that case).  Otherwise one fresh dict per checkpoint is returned sorted
710	    ascending by ``id`` with the fixed key order ``audit``, ``id``,
711	    ``stage``, ``state``, ``status``; the first four values are copied from
712	    the checkpoint and ``status`` is one of ``recoverable``, ``committed``
713	    or ``conflict``.
714	
715	    Let ``S`` mean the main state file holds a complete valid state whose
716	    canonical bytes hash to the state digest, ``A`` mean a valid audit
717	    chain contains a record whose hash is the audit digest, ``R0`` mean no
718	    receipt is bound under the id and ``R1`` mean that receipt binds
719	    exactly both digests.  A ``prepared`` checkpoint with ``not A and R0``,
720	    a ``state`` checkpoint with ``S and R0`` and an ``audit`` checkpoint
721	    with ``S and A and (R0 or R1)`` are ``recoverable``; a ``committed``
722	    checkpoint with ``S and A and R1`` is ``committed``; every other
723	    combination is ``conflict``.
724	
725	    No file is created or modified.  Type violations raise
726	    :class:`TypeError` and a bad path key set raises :class:`ValueError`;
727	    when at least one of the state main/backup files exists but neither
728	    holds a valid state, :class:`CorruptStateError` propagates unchanged,
729	    as do :class:`CorruptAuditError`, :class:`CorruptReceiptError`,
730	    :class:`CorruptTransactionError` and :class:`OSError`.
731	    """
732	    path_map = _validated_paths(paths)
733	
734	    records = _read_index(path_map[_CHECKPOINT])
735	    if not records:
736	        return []
737	
738	    audit_records = _audit._read_all_records(path_map[AUDIT])
739	    receipts_by_id = {
740	        receipt[ID]: receipt for receipt in _receipt._read_index(path_map[_RECEIPT])
741	    }
742	    main_state_bytes = _main_state_canonical_bytes(path_map[STATE])
743	    _assert_state_loadable(path_map[STATE])
744	
745	    audit_hashes = {record[_audit.HASH] for record in audit_records}
746	
747	    items: list[dict[str, str]] = []
748	    for record in records:
749	        state_digest = record[STATE]
750	        audit_digest = record[AUDIT]
751	        state_matches = (
752	            main_state_bytes is not None
753	            and hashlib.sha256(main_state_bytes).hexdigest() == state_digest
754	        )
755	        audit_ok = audit_digest in audit_hashes
756	        receipt = receipts_by_id.get(record[ID])
757	        status = _inspect_status(
758	            record[STAGE], state_matches, audit_ok, receipt,
759	            state_digest, audit_digest,
760	        )
761	        items.append(
762	            {
763	                AUDIT: audit_digest,
764	                ID: record[ID],
765	                STAGE: record[STAGE],
766	                STATE: state_digest,
767	                STATUS: status,
768	            }
769	        )
770	    return items
771

773	def commit(paths: dict[str, str], request: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]:
774	    """Run one replayable commit across storage, audit, receipt and checkpoint.
775	
776	    ``paths`` must contain exactly the str keys ``checkpoint``, ``state``,
777	    ``audit`` and ``receipt``.  ``request`` must contain exactly the keys
778	    ``id`` (same format as :func:`checkpoint`), ``state`` (a state obeying
779	    the :mod:`~offline_coordination.merge` state contract) and ``event``
780	    (an event obeying the :mod:`~offline_coordination.audit` event
781	    contract).
782	
783	    The state digest is the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of the complete
784	    canonical state bytes (including the trailing ``\\n``) that
785	    :mod:`~offline_coordination.storage` persists; the audit digest is
786	    the hash of the single audit record appended for this commit.  A
787	    first commit saves the state, appends exactly one audit event, binds
788	    a receipt carrying the id and both digests, and advances the
789	    checkpoint through ``prepared``, ``state``, ``audit`` and
790	    ``committed`` in that order.
791	
792	    Replaying the same arguments -- or re-entering after an interruption
793	    -- resumes at the recorded stage and performs each remaining side
794	    effect at most once, so the result is identical and no effect is
795	    duplicated.  Every artifact is reconciled against the checkpoint
796	    stage before any file is touched: a digest conflict, or a stage
797	    whose state file, audit record or receipt is missing, extra or
798	    mismatched, raises :class:`ValueError` and leaves the files
799	    unchanged.
800	
801	    On success a brand-new dict is returned with the key order
802	    ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage``, ``state`` and ``stage`` equal to
803	    ``committed``.  Type violations raise :class:`TypeError`; bad key
804	    sets, formats, state/event values, digest conflicts and stage/
805	    artifact mismatches raise :class:`ValueError`;
806	    :class:`CorruptStateError`, :class:`CorruptAuditError`,
807	    :class:`CorruptReceiptError`, :class:`CorruptTransactionError` and
808	    :class:`OSError` propagate unchanged.
809	    """
810	    (
811	        path_map,
812	        checkpoint_id,
813	        state,
814	        event,
815	        payload,
816	    ) = _validated_commit_inputs(paths, request)
817	    checkpoint_path = path_map[_CHECKPOINT]
818	    state_path = path_map[STATE]
819	    audit_path = path_map[AUDIT]
820	    receipt_path = path_map[_RECEIPT]
821	
822	    state_digest = hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
823	
824	    # Read every artifact up front.  All reconciliation below happens
825	    # before any mutation, so a rejected commit changes nothing.
826	    audit_records = _audit._read_all_records(audit_path)
